messages:
sarah: Heads up — saw a sharp uptick in ECC corrected errors from apac-pool-3 starting ~08:12 UTC. Sparse but rising across multiple cards (gpu0,gpu2,gpu5). Noting latency bump on a couple pods.
raj: Got the alert. Any Xid OOMs or just correctables?
sarah: Only correctables so far, no Xid in logs. Dashboard: error rate 5x baseline over last 15m.
ops-bot: [alert] ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE apac-pool-3 — 08:14 UTC — 320 events in 15m — severity: medium
chen: Can you paste the raw query you used? want to cross-check with event-window aggregation.
sarah: Sure: ```promql
sum(rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total{pool="apac-pool-3"}[5m])) by (card)
```
chen: Thx. My read — distribution across cards suggests noisy interconnect rather than single-card failing.
alex: Important decision: do we kick in a hard drain at threshold T1 or attempt staged mitigation to avoid capacity churn? cost + warmup = >10% request latency if we reassign too many jobs.
maya: Proposing a 3-stage guardrail:
  1) Detect: 3x baseline sustained over 10m -> start verbose telemetry + tag node
  2) Mitigate: if 5x over 15m, cordon new allocations and reduce batch sizes on current workers
  3) Evacuate: if 10x over 30m OR Xid appears -> soft-evacuate (graceful requeue), then mark for replacement
This avoids immediate full-drain.
raj: How do we implement "soft-evacuate"? current drain tooling is binary (drain or leave).
chen: We can add a pre-evac probe that sets node.k8s/evac-mode=soft and triggers graceful pod migration with extended timeout. Pseudocode:
```yaml
- set label node/evac-mode: soft
- patch deployments with pod disruption budget strategy: maxUnavailable: 1
- scale down batch worker concurrency by 50% via configmap roll
```
alex: Also need a hysteresis window to prevent flip-flopping: require the spike to be above threshold for N minutes after any reduction before evicting.
maya: Exactly. In simulation (see sim-bot results below), staged approach prevented 4 unnecessary hardware replacements across test fleet.
sim-bot: Simulation summary: workload=chat-gen, 200 nodes, injected intermittent ECC bursts on 6% of cards. Hard-drain policy -> 32 nodes replaced, 12% SLA misses. Graded policy -> 8 nodes replaced, 2% SLA misses.
raj: Solid. What about region constraints? apac-pool-3 has limited spare capacity. Evacuating 10% would push jobs to eu-west and increase egress.
sarah: We should consider capacity-aware fallback: if target region available capacity < threshold, delay evacuation and escalate to oncall.
chen: Agreed. Proposed rule:
  - If evac would exceed regional spare-capacity threshold (5%), create urgent incident and run topological fallback: prioritize lower-cost model variants for migrated workloads.
alex: We need an operational playbook update. Short checklist for oncall:
  - Confirm correctables vs uncorrectable
  - Run quick health-check script: `ssh node && nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc`
  - Apply soft-evac label
  - Monitor for hysteresis window (30m)
  - If Xid or temperature rise -> full drain and replace
maya: I can draft the playbook and add the soft-evac mutating webhook to the infra repo. Will also add a metric for "evac-delay-seconds" so we can measure decision latency.
ops-bot: Added incident channel #inc-ecc-apac and created runbook stub: https://confluence/internal/apac-ecc
sarah: Quick ask — can infra add an automated experiment that tries the staged mitigation on a small percentage (2%) of noisy nodes to validate in prod safely?
chen: Yes — feature flagged rollout. We'll gate by pool and percentage.
raj: One more: ensure billing/cost tracker tags migrations so we can estimate cross-region egress cost from emergency evacs.
alex: I'll add a cost alert integration and update the console to show projected evict cost before human approves.
sarah: Great. Action items:
  - maya: draft playbook + webhook (ETA EOD)
  - chen: implement soft-evac label logic + feature flag (ETA 48h)
  - alex: cost projection UI change (ETA next week)
  - raj: add billing tags and egress alert (ETA 48h)
  - sim-bot/chen: run canary sim at 2% in apac (ETA 24h)
maya: On it. Posting draft in #eng-infra once ready.
sarah: Thanks all. Will keep monitoring; if we see Xid or uncorrectable, escalate immediately. :thumbsup:
